jurisdiction.name: New Zealand
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: New Zealand takes a light-touch, principles-based approach with no AI-specific law: the 2025 AI Strategy and Responsible AI Guidance for Businesses from the business ministry (MBIE), the Public Service AI Framework and generative AI guidance from the Government Chief Digital Officer, and the 2020 Algorithm Charter signed by government agencies. The Privacy Act 2020 applies to AI, the Privacy Commissioner has issued AI guidance and the binding Biometric Processing Privacy Code 2025, and the Ministry for Regulation has guidance for regulators on AI. A member's bill on deepfakes is before a select committee.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
Department of Internal Affairs (Government Chief Digital Officer)
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The Privacy Act is recorded as located only, and the deepfake bill and the education ministry's AI guidance are listed as leads. Not yet verified from the official text: the full text of the Privacy Act.

instruments.summary: New Zealand's first national AI strategy, subtitled 'Accelerating Private Sector AI Adoption and Innovation', issued by MBIE with a foreword by the Minister of Science, Innovation and Technology. It sets out barriers to AI uptake and government actions (stable and enabling policy, demystifying AI for business, building capability) and states a light-touch, principles-based approach that relies on existing law (privacy, consumer protection, human rights) and on the OECD AI Principles rather than new AI-specific legislation.

instruments.summary: Guidance from the Ministry for Regulation for New Zealand regulatory agencies on adopting AI in regulatory practice. It covers low-risk starting points, capability building, working with AI vendors, human-in-the-loop requirements for high-stakes or rights-affecting decisions, iterative scaling and ethical use drawn from public-sector frameworks. Version 1.1 adds resources on Māori data and Māori data sovereignty.

instruments.summary: A commitment by signatory government agencies to use algorithms in a fair, ethical and transparent way. Using a risk matrix, signatories focus on algorithms with high impact on people and commit to transparency, partnership (Te Tiriti o Waitangi), engaging people, data quality and bias checks, privacy, ethics and human rights safeguards, and human oversight with avenues to challenge decisions.

instruments.summary: Privacy Commissioner guidance stating that the Privacy Act 2020 applies to everyone using AI tools in New Zealand and explaining how each Information Privacy Principle applies across the AI lifecycle, from training data to outputs. It expects agencies to do a privacy impact assessment before using AI tools, to check accuracy and fairness (including engagement with Māori), to keep prompts and training data secure, and to keep human review of AI outputs.

instruments.current_status: Issued 21 July 2025; in force 3 November 2025, with a transition period for existing biometric users that ended 3 August 2026. Amendment No 1 (March 2026) reflects new IPP3A; consolidated text in force from 1 May 2026.
instruments.summary: Code of practice made by the Privacy Commissioner under the Privacy Act 2020 that sets binding privacy rules for organisations collecting and using biometric information in automated biometric processing such as facial recognition. It modifies the privacy principles for biometric information covering collection, use, disclosure, access and correction requests, and storage, security, retention and disposal of biometric information.

instruments.summary: New Zealand's general data protection law, with Information Privacy Principles that govern collection, use, disclosure and security of personal information, including in AI training and use. It is enforced by the Privacy Commissioner, who may issue binding codes of practice such as the Biometric Processing Privacy Code 2025.

instruments.english_title: Cyber readiness in the Frontier AI era
instruments.current_status: NCSC guidance page, published date 4 June 2026 as printed on the page. The page frames the advice as whole-of-government advice built on existing NCSC technical advice and the Protective Security Requirements; it does not itself state that it is binding.
instruments.summary: NCSC advisory for New Zealand government cyber security decision-makers on preparing for frontier AI products, which it describes as raising the speed and scale of attacks on known vulnerabilities. It asks agencies to treat as an immediate priority assuring compliance with the NZISM, the NCSC Cyber Security Framework, the Minimum Cyber Security Standards and the Protective Security Requirements, confirming executive accountability for frontier AI cyber risk, and remediating gaps. It links the practical guidance 'How to Act Now to Prepare for Frontier AI'.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: New Zealand's legislation portal, parliament, government agencies, ministries and regulators were searched. No AI-specific Act was found, a member's bill on deepfakes is listed as a lead, and there was no material for standards, sandboxes, indices, drafts, international instruments or older publications. The central bank, the financial markets regulator and the competition regulator were only briefly searched, so these, the legislation portal and the education ministry's AI page remain to be checked.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. legislation.govt.nz returned HTTP 202 empty/403 (Privacy Act located only; commencement from the Privacy Commissioner's site). MBIE intermittently bot-protected (business guidance PDF read from the 2026-10-11 download). Ministry sweeps for justice, defence, Treasury/IRD and MSD were a single combined search; RBNZ, FMA and Commerce Commission one shallow pass. New Zealand is not a party to Convention 108. Units covered: Law: Legislation portal (legislation.govt.nz) and Parliament searched: no AI-specific Act; Privacy Act 2020 recorded (located only, portal blocks automated clients) and Biometric Processing Privacy Code 2025 (OPC); Deepfake Digital Harm and Exploitation Bill (member's bill, 2025) held as a lead. No public-sector algorithm statute found.; Government: MBIE (AI Strategy 2025, Responsible AI Guidance for Businesses), DIA/GCDO (Public Service AI Framework, GenAI guidance), Stats NZ (Algorithm Charter 2020), Ministry for Regulation (Responsible AI in Action).; Ministries: Health NZ (NAIAEAG GenAI/LLM rules) recorded; Ministry of Education GenAI page located but unreadable (lead); justice, defence, Treasury/IRD, MSD: searched, nothing AI-specific found.; Regulators: Privacy Commissioner (AI and IPPs guidance; biometrics code) and NCSC (joint AI guidance) recorded; RBNZ, FMA, Commerce Commission: searched, no AI-specific document found in this pass.. Not reached: Ministry of Education generative AI page (unreadable); Detailed sweep of RBNZ/FMA/Commerce Commission sites; Standards NZ adoption of ISO/IEC 42001 (not checked). Could not verify: Privacy Act 2020 full text on legislation.govt.nz (HTTP 202 empty / 403); Exact launch day of the AI Strategy (MBIE news page blocked; PDF says July 2025); Ministry of Education GenAI guidance. standards, sandbox, index-readiness, drafts, international, historical: no material found.
